title.narrative: Oxfam-IBIS Support Mechanism for Indigenous Peoples, "Oxlajuj Tz'ikin" 2019-2025

description.narrative: The project aims to promote the exercise of indigenous peoples' individual and collective rights in accordance with international standards, and to strengthen the ability of indigenous people to contribute to the development and implementation of national laws, institutional frameworks and public policies.

The indigenous peoples of Guatemala are subject to racism, discrimination and social, economic and political marginalization, which among other things has led to significantly higher poverty and illiteracy among indigenous peoples compared to the rest of the population, indigenous peoples have the lowest social indicators in the country.
"The programme for indigenous people's rights" is implementeded by Oxfam-Ibis together with 16 partner organizations aims to contribute to the exercise of the individual and collective rights, and self-determination of indigenous people in accordance with international agreements. The programme will cover 11 of Guatemala's 22 administrative regions (Totonicapán, Sololá, Quetzaltenango, Alta and Baja Verapaz, Quiche, Santa Rosa, Jutiapa, Jalapa, Chimaltenango and Guatemala City). These areas are highly affected by poverty and exclusion.
The Swedish contribution will be used for activities aimed at strengthening knowledge and exercise of individual and collective rights as well as strengthening the capacities of the partner organisations. Legal support will be provided through the project to support indigenous people to claim their rights as established in national legislation and international agreements. The indigenous justice system will be strengthened in order to ensure equal justice for women and men. Through the facilitation of a dialogue for the integration of a gender perspective in work with indigenous authorities women’s participation in decision-making processes is expected to increase. Work with men and boys will be used as a strategy to prevent violence against women, teenage pregnancies and child marriages. As a conflict prevention measure, indigenous organizations will be supported in improving their capacity to deal with internal conflicts within their own communities, and for stronger influence on social issues, relationships with state institutions at local and national level will be supported.
The project will have a strong focus on alliance building with other civil society organisations, state and academic institutions, as well as with the UN Human Rights Office to further strengthen the implementation and sustainability of the results. In this work, actors defending human rights are expected to work together in areas such as the environment and climate, access to justice and gender equality for an increased impact.
Oxfam-IBIS has applied to Sida for funding of 60 million SEK to carry out the project in Guatemala during the period during November 2019 - April 2023. The project's total budget is 66.3 million SEK, out of which 6.3 million SEK is financed by DANIDA. Approximately 44 million SEK (66%) of the project budget will be forwarded to 16 local indigenous organizations.

Urfolken i Guatemala är utsatta för rasism, diskriminering och social, ekonomisk och politisk marginalisering vilket bland annat har lett till betydande högre fattigdom och analfabetism bland urfolk jämfört med resten av befolkningen, urfolk har de lägsta sociala indikatorerna i landet.
"Programmet för urfolksrättigheter" genomförs av Oxfam-Ibis tillsammans med 16 partnerorganisationer och syftar till att bidra till utövandet av urfolks individuella och kollektiva rättigheter, samt självbestämmande i enlighet med internationella överenskommelser. Programmet kommer att täcka 11 av landets 22 regiondepartement (Totonicapán, Sololá, Quetzaltenango, Alta och Baja Verapaz, Quiche, Santa Rosa, Jutiapa, Jalapa, Chimaltenango och Guatemala City. Dessa områden påverkas starkt av fattigdom och exkludering.
Det svenska bidraget kommer att användas för aktiviteter som syftar till att stärka kunskapen om och utövandet av individuella och kollektiva rättigheter samt stärka partnerorganisationernas kapacitet. I projektet ingår juridiskt stöd för att urfolk ska kunna kräva sina rättigheter enligt nationell lagstiftning och internationella avtal. Även urfolks eget rättssystem kommer att stärkas för att säkerställa jämställd rättvisa mellan kvinnor och män. Genom att underlätta dialog för integrering av ett jämställdhetsperspektiv i arbetet med urfolksmyndigheter förväntas kvinnors deltagande i beslutsprocesser öka. Arbete med män och pojkar kommer att användas som strategi för att förebygga våld mot kvinnor, tonårsgraviditeter och barnäktenskap. I konfliktförebyggande syfte kommer urfolksorganisationer stödjas i att förbättra sin kapacitet att hantera interna konflikter inom sina egna samhällen, och för stärkt inflytande i samhällsfrågor kommer relationsbyggande med statliga institutioner på lokal och nationell nivå stödjas.
Projektet kommer att ha ett starkt fokus på alliansbyggande med andra civilsamhällesorganisationer, statliga och akademiska institutioner, samt med FN's kontor för mänskliga rättigheter för att ytterligare stärka genomförandet och hållbarheten i resultaten. Inom detta arbete förväntas aktörer som försvarar de mänskliga rättigheterna organisera sig för större genomslag inom områden som till exempel miljö- och klimat, tillgång till rättvisa och jämställdhet.
Oxfam-IBIS har ansökt om finansiering av 60 miljoner kr för att genomföra projektet i Guatemala under perioden november 2019 - april 2023. Projektets totala budget är 66,3 miljoner kr, varav 6,3 miljoner kr finansieras av DANIDA. Cirka 44 miljoner kr (66%) av projektbudgeten vidareförmedlas till 16 lokala urfolksorganisationer.

The program has been successful in supporting development of governance models for land and forests based on perspectives of indigenous peoples. It has also been successful by supporting access to justice in both systems (the national legal system and the indigenous authorities local application of law based on Mayan cosmovision and traditional practices).
The program has supported gender equality strengthening women participation in decision making within indigenous people´s organizations. The program has also provided training to reduce violence against women. The program has worked to reduce domestic violence against women, supporting women and girls accessing the national legal system in cases of domestic violence, including unwanted pregnancies in girls and young women caused by sexual violence, which is frequent in rural indigenous communities.
Some examples of achieved results as per bilateral cooperation strategy objectives include:
1.2 Greater gender equality, including the reduction of gender-based violence, as well as access to and respect for health and sexual and reproductive rights.
Regarding the rights of indigenous women, national data shows that 45.7% of urban women and 57.4% of rural women agree that women should be responsible for the care of children, the sick and the elderly. Of these, 47% of young women between the ages of 15 and 29 also agree. For Guatemala, these issues are pending challenges due to lack of solid institutional framework, lack of updated policy instruments based on the current needs and interests of indigenous women, and even more so, their limited participation in decision-making spaces.
Oxfam dedicated efforts to the organization and role of indigenous midwifes whereby 620 organized midwives are monitoring implementation of the National Midwife Policy, influencing decision-making in the executive and legislative branches to ensure that the policy strengthens access to health care through the indigenous peoples' own health care system.
Area 2 - Environment and climate: sustainable development, sustainable management of ecosystems and biodiversity, and sustainable use of natural resources
2.1 Sustainable use and management of natural resources, ecosystems, and biodiversity, including nature-based solutions for climate change adaptation and economic development.
Various studies show that Indigenous Peoples safeguard 80% of biodiversity, and that forest lands under collective management of local communities and Indigenous Peoples contain at least a quarter of all above-ground carbon in tropical and subtropical forests. However, it's the indigenous communities that bear the greatest impacts from loss of biodiversity and impact of climate change. Their ancestral knowledge and experiences are essential for adapting to, mitigating and reducing climate and disaster risks. The narrative report indicates that Indigenous authorities have strengthened their commitment to the preservation of their lands, territories and natural resources. Given the lack of legislation ensuring full respect for the administration of their territory, they have embarked on a quest for peaceful solutions in specific cases, exhausting existing legal mechanisms, including inter-community political dialogue and dialogue with public authorities. In the exercise of their duties, the Indigenous authorities also ensure the balance of power in their territories. To this end, governance is one of the fundamental elements in their communities. Therefore, the search for solutions to various conflict situations in their territories, such as the management of communal forests, territorial delimitation and communal property, are part of their work.
In 2024, three governance models for indigenous peoples' communal lands and forests were strengthened, and actions have been implemented to promote resilience to climate change by improving technical capacities, sharing experiences, raising awareness on environmental issues and reforesting 10 hectares in communities in the Ixcán region through community reforestation campaigns and protecting 2,200 hectares of communal forests in Totonicapán.
Additionally, a Municipal Environmental Policy of Ixcán, Department of Quiché, was approved.
Area 3 Inclusive Economic Development
3.1 Enhance/promote economic activities for income generation and develop inclusive and sustainable markets with productive employment potential, ensuring management
High levels of poverty and inequality, structural discrimination and corruption limit access to fundamental rights, especially for groups that have historically faced exclusion, including Indigenous peoples, Afro-descendant communities and rural communities. According to official figures, 56% of the population lived in poverty in 2023, including 16% in extreme poverty, according to the national poverty line. To improve Indigenous Peoples, especially women, income generating opportunities, the program has supported the organizational and economic autonomy of 350 indigenous women through promotion of agroecological productive initiatives and access to alternative markets. Nine political and legal instruments were negotiated that benefit indigenous populations economically and socially.
Business sustainability was promoted through the design of an online store, trademark registration, participation in national exhibitions, legal incorporation of their organization and innovation of artisan and commercial processes with the Santiago Atitlán Consortium of Associations.
